content.title: Duke vs UConn highlights: Huskies complete stunning comeback vs Blue Devils in Elite 8
content.text: Updated March 29, 2026, 9:39 p.m. ETThe final 2026 Final Four spot came down to the marquee Elite Eight matchup between Duke and UConn. And boy, did it not disappoint.For most of the game it looked like Duke was headed back to another Final Four, building a 19-point lead. But UConn kept chipping away and stole the game — literally — in the final seconds.Down two points with only seconds to play, UConn forced a turnover at midcourt, and the ball ended up in the hands of freshman Braylon Mullins, who launched a long 3-pointer that hit nothing but net with just tenths of a second remaining to give the Huskies a stunning 73-72 win.Here's how the game unfolded:HIT REFRESH FOR UPDATES. UConn vs Duke basketball scoreThis section will be updated throughout the game.TEAMS1H2HFUConn294473Duke442872 Duke vs UConn basketball highlights Duke vs UConn basketball updatesThis section will be updated throughout the game.UConn completes comeback, stuns DukeAfter trailing by as many as 17 in the second half, UConn is headed to the Final Four after Braylon Mullins buries a deep 3 with 0.4 seconds remaining to deliver the Huskies a 73-72 win against Duke in the Elite Eight.Mullins had missed all four of his attempts from 3 before his destined-to-be-iconic game-winner. After missing 17 of their first 18 3s against Duke, the Huskies finished the game making four of their final five shots from beyond the arc.There's an added wrinkle that's just perfect for March, too — Mullins is from Greenfield, Indiana, about 25 miles away from downtown Indianapolis, where next week's Final Four will be held.The victory sends UConn to its third Final Four in the past four years. There, the Huskies will take on No. 3 seed Illinois, with the winner of that game advancing to take on No. 1 seed Arizona or No. 1 seed Michigan in the national title game.Duke, UConn going down to the wireAfter Michigan's blowout of Tennessee earlier today, we've got a compelling final game of the Elite Eight, with Duke leading UConn 65-58 with about six minutes to go. The Huskies missed 17 of their first 18 3-pointers, but got treys on back-to-back possessions from Silas Demary Jr. to get within seven.As a wise man once said, hold on to your butts.UConn clawing back against DukeCoach Dan Hurley's team is starting to show why its vying for its third championship in the past four years. After trailing by 17 with 17 minutes left, UConn is on a 16-6 run to get within seven, 56-49, with 10:59 remaining.The Huskies are shooting 53.3% from the field in the half, including 80% from inside the 3-point arc. Tarris Reed Jr. has 11 of UConn's 20 points this half. Duke up 15 on UConn at halftimeThe Blue Devils are 20 minutes away from continuing their national championship dreams, with a 44-29 lead on UConn at halftime. Duke led by 19 with 3:24 remaining in the half before the Huskies carved into the deficit a bit before heading to the locker room.It's UConn's largest halftime deficit in a game this season.Cam Boozer's been superb for coach Jon Scheyer's team, with 14 points, five rebounds, three assists and two blocks while his twin brother, Cayden, has been pretty good himself, with 13 points and two steals. Tarris Reed Jr. has a team-high 12 points and two blocks for UConn, though he will start the second half with two fouls.Duke shot 51.7% from the field while UConn made just 12 of their 34 field-goal attempts (35.3%), including one of its 11 3-pointers.Duke up early on UConnWith a second-consecutive trip to the Final Four on the line, Duke has come out firing, with a 30-21 lead over UConn with 7:29 remaining in their first half of their Elite Eight matchup in Washington, D.C.Likely national player of the year Cam Boozer is leading the way with nine points for the Blue Devils, who are shooting 60% from the field. Caleb Foster injury updateAfter playing in his first game since suffering a broken foot, Caleb Foster played 19 minutes in Duke's Sweet 16 win against St. John's on Friday. He isn't in the starting lineup today for the Blue Devils, but he's expected to play in the Elite Eight against UConn.What time is Duke vs UConn in Elite 8?Time: 5:05 p.m. ET, Sunday, March 29.What channel is Duke vs UConn? How to watch, streaming infoThe game is airing on CBS, streaming via Paramount+.Duke vs UConn Elite 8 prediction, odds∎ Anna Snyder, Fayetteville Observer: Duke 70, UConn 68Expect a physical, back-and-forth game, but with Caleb Foster back in the rotation, Duke has just enough offensive balance to edge UConn and make its way back to the Final Four.Austin Curtright: UConnJohn Leuzzi: DukeJordan Mendoza: DukeEhsan Kassim: UConnMoneyline: Duke (-220); UConn (+180)Spread: Duke (-5.5)Over/under total: 133.5Duke will reach Final Four if...John Leuzzi: It can keep UConn's offense out of rhythm.Jordan Mendoza: Out-muscles Connecticut.Ehsan Kassim: Cam Boozer takes over.Austin Curtright: If contains Tarris Reed Jr.UConn will reach Final Four if...John Leuzzi: Tarris Reed Jr. continues to impact the paint.Jordan Mendoza: It shoots lights out.Ehsan Kassim: It can continue to get Duke to turn the ball over.Austin Curtright: Its bench can keep up with Duke's deep rotation.Caleb Foster injury update: Will Duke guard play vs UConn?Twenty days after Foster fractured his right foot in a win against North Carolina, he returned to play Friday against St. John's.Foster came off the bench to score 11 points, corral three rebounds and dish out a pair of assists across 19 crucial minutes to spark the No. 1 Blue Devils’ 80-75 win against No. 5 St. John’s to reach the East Region finals.He rolled out of the Duke locker room with his right foot wrapped in ice and his right knee perched atop a one-legged scooter, a bag of ice strapped and wrapped around his left calf for good measure."He's doing well. For us, he's not doing anything on the court (Saturday)," Scheyer said. "Even for these guys, it's been more of a walk-through day getting ready. First time playing in a few weeks, he's sore and recovering like you would expect, but nothing concerning."Cameron Boozer NBA draft stock, mock draft predictionsBoozer is widely projected as a top-3 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. Here’s a look at where various mock drafts from major outlets have the Duke freshman going:USA TODAY (as of March 13): No. 3 overall to the Sacramento KingsESPN (as of March 11): No. 3 overall to the Indiana PacersCBS Sports (as of March 17): No. 3 overall to the Brooklyn NetsIs Cameron Boozer related to Carlos Boozer?Cameron Boozer and his twin brother, Cayden (also a freshman for Duke) are the sons of former NBA All-Star Carlos Boozer.Before his 13-year career in the NBA, Carlos Boozer was a standout forward for the Blue Devils under Mike Krzyzewski from 1999-2002. A member of Duke's 2001 national championship team, Carlos Boozer finished his three-year career with the Blue Devils with more than 1,500 points scored and started 93 of the 101 games in which he appeared.How old is Alex Karaban? How long has Alex Karaban been at UConn?Karaban is 23 years old and enrolled at UConn in 2022. He was part of the Huskies' 2023 and 2024 national championship teams.Braylon Mullins 2026 NBA Draft, mock draft predictionNo. 29 overall to Cleveland Cavaliers.Kalbrosky's Analysis:Braylon Mullins, a five-star recruit and former McDonald's All American, missed the start of the season due to an ankle injury. But he has returned to action for the Huskies and has shown what makes him such an appealing player. He is a useful off-ball threat, which gives him an immediately practical role at the next level. The Big East All-Freshman wing shot 40.7 percent on 3-pointers during his first 18 games in the starting lineup, but it may be tough for scouts to forget his 0-for-8 performance from beyond the arc during his first game in March Madness.See USA TODAY's full mock draft hereBraylon Mullins stats(all stats as of March 15)12 points per game3.5 rebounds per game1.4 assists per game43.5% field goal percentage34.5% three-point field goal percentage
